response.sql:
WITH pair_averages AS (
  SELECT
    f.orderslink,
    u.acctscope,
    AVG(f.feerate) AS avg_fee_rate
  FROM fees AS f
  JOIN orders AS o
    ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  JOIN users AS u
    ON o.userlink = u.userstamp
  GROUP BY f.orderslink, u.acctscope
),
mean_average AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_fee_rate) AS mean_pair_avg
  FROM pair_averages
),
above_mean AS (
  SELECT
    p.orderslink,
    p.acctscope,
    p.avg_fee_rate,
    p.avg_fee_rate - m.mean_pair_avg AS excess
  FROM pair_averages AS p
  CROSS JOIN mean_average AS m
  WHERE p.avg_fee_rate > m.mean_pair_avg
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    orderslink,
    acctscope,
    avg_fee_rate,
    excess,
    RANK() OVER (
      PARTITION BY acctscope
      ORDER BY excess DESC
    ) AS scope_rank
  FROM above_mean
)
SELECT
  orderslink,
  acctscope,
  avg_fee_rate,
  excess,
  scope_rank
FROM ranked
WHERE scope_rank <= 3
ORDER BY acctscope, scope_rank, orderslink;

assumptions.assumption: Ties in excess share a rank, so the top three rank positions can include more than three pairs in a scope.

alternatives.interpretation: If you mean exactly three pairs per scope, including a deterministic tie-break by orderslink, use ROW_NUMBER instead of RANK and filter to row numbers at most 3.
